subject: [HealthCore] Evidence handoff for audit/access logs — export integrity, residency, and proof-of-deletion
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@healthcore.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthcore.com>, dpo@healthcore.com
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence handoff: audit/access logs export capabilities and deletion proof

Hi Mateo,

We're preparing for a regulatory data request and need to understand Redwood's capabilities for handing over audit/access logs for our tenant. A few specifics from our side: 

- Objective: export a contiguous window of tenant audit logs (user activity + admin actions) for e-discovery and for our legal hold.
- Residency: we need exported data that clearly maps to the region of origin (EU vs US) and a manifest with region tags.
- Formats: preference for a columnar, schematized format (Parquet or compressed JSONL) that we can ingest to our data lake.
- Integrity: we require an integrity manifest (file list + sha256 checksums) and a signed statement that the extract matches the set of records for the period.
- Deletion proof: for records deleted later, we need a deletion attestation/certificate and an audit indicating when/why deletion occurred.
- Delivery: S3 presigned URL or secure transfer to our org bucket.

Can you confirm what Redwood supports today (formats, manifest, checksums, region tagging), typical lead time for a 90-day contiguous export, and whether you can provide a deletion certification for items removed after the snapshot?

Thanks — attaching a short scope doc separately.

Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Privacy Program Manager
HealthCore Inc.

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@healthcore.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthcore.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence handoff: audit/access logs export capabilities and deletion proof

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear scope. High level answers up front, followed by a short runbook and a couple of clarifying questions.

What we support today:
- Formats: Parquet (columnar, recommended) and gzipped JSONL. Parquet is our default for large exports — schema included.
- Delivery: S3 presigned PUT to your bucket, or we can upload to a customer-provided secure SFTP/GCS location.
- Integrity: export includes a manifest.csv with file-level sha256 checksums and a top-level export.json metadata file containing region mapping, extract start/end timestamps (ISO8601), and export UTC hash. We can also timestamp-sign the export metadata with our key.
- Region tagging: each exported file includes a header field region= (us/eu/apac) and exported records include a region_code field where applicable; manifest groups files by region.
- Deletion attestation: for deletions after the snapshot we provide a deletion manifest (tombstone list) and an attestation letter that includes deletion timestamps, requester, and policy reason. For legal hold scenarios we can freeze deletion for the tenant on request and provide a hold-id for traceability.

Lead time & SLA:
- Typical turnaround for a 90-day contiguous export: 3–5 business days for standard priority; 24–48 hours for expedited (paid) requests depending on retention size.
- Delivery verification: we run a validation pass and provide an export integrity report.

Runbook (short):
1) Confirm the extract window and whether you require full request bodies or redacted payloads.
2) Agree on delivery method + KMS: default server-side AES256; optional customer-managed KMS if needed.
3) We stage the extract, run checksum, produce manifest.csv + export.json, package as .tar.gz (or multi-file), and hand to you via agreed channel.
4) Provide deletion attestation if requested; generate tombstone manifest if records were removed within X window.

Questions from our side:
- Do you need request/response bodies in raw form, or are obfuscated identifiers acceptable for e-discovery?
- For the deletion attestation, do you need a per-record proof or a signed bulk attestation?

I've attached an export_manifest_template.csv that shows the fields we include. If that looks good I can loop in our infra engineer to schedule a test extract next week.

— Mateo Alvarez
Customer Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attached: export_manifest_template.csv)

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@healthcore.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthcore.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence handoff: audit/access logs export capabilities and deletion proof

Thanks Mateo — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

> Do you need request/response bodies in raw form, or are obfuscated identifiers acceptable for e-discovery?

Legal wants request metadata and full request paths (URLs + query params) but bodies only when they contain PII flags; for those, we'd prefer pseudonymized user ids. Can Redwood include an indicator column (pii_flag: true/false) and optionally include the raw body in a separate encrypted file set if we sign a DPA amendment?

Also please confirm:
- Will the export include actor (admin vs end-user) and the auth identity (service account vs user id)?
- If we request a deletion attestation, we need it per-account (account id) with timestamps and the operator id. Bulk attestation is acceptable only if it includes a checksum mapping to the exported snapshot.

If those are possible, let's plan a test extract for Wed 2028-06-06. Can you confirm capacity and whether we need an expedited request?

Sarah

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@healthcore.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-31T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence handoff: audit/access logs export capabilities and deletion proof

Hi Sarah — looping in Marissa from Compliance; brief answers and next steps below.

Quoted for context:
> Legal wants request metadata and full request paths (URLs + query params) but bodies only when they contain PII flags; for those, we'd prefer pseudonymized user ids. Can Redwood include an indicator column (pii_flag: true/false) and optionally include the raw body in a separate encrypted file set if we sign a DPA amendment?

Yes — we include the following by default in every exported event: timestamp_utc, region_code, tenant_id, account_id, actor_type (admin|user|service), actor_id (pseudonymized), action_type, resource_path, http_method, status_code, latency_ms.

PII and bodies:
- We add a pii_flag boolean when our detection heuristics surface potential PII.
- Raw request/response bodies are excluded from default exports; we can include them in a separate encrypted bundle (AES-256) with customer-managed KMS after a DPA amendment and scoping approval.

Deletion attestation:
- We can produce per-account deletion attestations (CSV) listing record_id, deletion_timestamp, operator_id, deletion_reason. Each attestation includes a signature block and maps to the exported snapshot via the export_id and checksums.

Delivery & encryption:
- Transit: TLS 1.3 for all handoff channels.
- At rest: server-side AES-256 by default; customer-managed KMS supported for S3 uploads.

Test extract scheduling:
- Wed 2028-06-06 is available. Standard priority should suffice for a 90-day snapshot under 100GB; if your estimated size is >100GB we recommend expedited (24–48h) for guaranteed window.

Next steps:
1) Sign the small export scope addendum (we'll email the DPA amendment if you opt for raw bodies).
2) Confirm extract window and estimated dataset size.
3) Send the destination bucket details and KMS ARN (if using CMK).
4) We'll run a dry-run and provide the sample parquet bundle (attached) before full extract.

Attaching: redwood-sample-export.parquet.gz (sample schema + small dataset).

— Kimberly Park
Senior Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
(attached: redwood-sample-export.parquet.gz)
